### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Brings every interior cell to phase equilibrium once per step, at fixed density and fixed internal
energy density, by moving mass between each vapour and its condensates; @eq-ch10-satadj-state.
**Data.** In: $\rho$, $\rho e$ and $y_n$ of each interior cell, cell averages. Out: the species rows
$\rho_n = \rho\,y_n$; $E$, momentum and $\rho_{\mathrm d}$ are not written.
**Placement.** Last RK stage, after the whole-column conserved limiter and before the boundary fill.
**Activation.** On whenever the thermo block declares reactions; no switch of its own. kintera's `uv-solver`,
`max-iter` and `ftol` tune the solve.
**Guarantee / limits.** $E$ exact; total water to the phase solve's tolerance; ghosts are not adjusted; a failed
cell stays unadjusted and raises redo cause 16.
**Evidence.** `test_wall_saturation` ($10^{-12}$ relative) and `satadj_check.py` `[C1]`–`[C3]`; the ctest was not
run at the pin.
:::

Phase change is fast compared with the dynamics, so snapy does not resolve it inside the RK stages. It lets the
stages advect vapour and condensate as tracers that carry their own reference energies, and once per step, after
the last stage has been averaged, it hands each interior cell to kintera's equilibrium solve at fixed volume and fixed internal energy density
solve (@sec-ch02-saturation) and writes the new mass fractions back. Latent heat is never a separate source: it is
the difference of the species reference energies $u^{\star}_n$ (NOTATION.md section 2), so moving mass between
phases at fixed $\rho e$ changes the temperature and leaves $E$ alone. This section is the snapy side of that solve:
when it runs, what it is handed, what it writes, and what happens when it fails.

The adjustment is on whenever the thermo block of the YAML card lists reactions; there is no flag to turn it off
while keeping the reactions. Its failures do not stop the step: they are counted and turned into redo cause 16
(@sec-ch10-redo). The ghost cells are not adjusted; the boundary fill that ends the stage refills the physical ghosts
from the adjusted interior.

### Derivation

The derivation of the equilibrium itself, its internal-energy-density constraint and its active-set solve, is
@sec-ch02-saturation; it is not repeated here. What this section adds is the state handed to it and the proof that
the write-back changes only the species rows.

Step (6) of the stage update, in `MeshBlockImpl::advance_local`, forms in every cell the total density, the internal
energy density and the mass fractions from the conserved state:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho &= \rho_{\mathrm{d}} + \sum_{n}\rho_n,\\
\rho e &= E - \tfrac12\rho\lvert\mathbf v\rvert^2,\\
y_n &= \rho_n/\rho .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch10-satadj-state}

@eq-ch10-satadj-state is formed as `rho`, `ie` and `yfrac`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}), with the kinetic energy from the equation of
state's `U->K`. kintera's `ThermoYImpl::forward` receives $\rho$ and $\rho e$ by value and $y_n$ by reference, solves
the equilibrium at fixed $\rho$ and fixed $\rho e$, and overwrites $y_n$
([`kintera thermo_y.cpp:275-383`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L275-L383)).
snapy then writes $\rho_n \leftarrow \rho\,y_n$ for every species row, with the same $\rho$ it handed in
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).

Three consequences follow from these lines alone. First, the energy row is not written, so $E$ is unchanged to the
last bit; since momentum is not written either, $\rho e = E - \tfrac12\rho\lvert\mathbf v\rvert^2$ is unchanged as
long as $\rho$ is. Second, the dry row is not written, so $\rho_{\mathrm{d}}$ is unchanged. Third, $\rho$ is
unchanged if and only if $\sum_n y_n$ is: the phase reactions move mass between species rows and never create it,
so kintera returns fractions whose sum equals the input sum up to its solver tolerance, and $\rho$ after the
write-back equals $\rho$ before to that tolerance. The energy is therefore conserved exactly and the total water to
the tolerance of the phase solve; `test_wall_saturation` asserts both below $10^{-12}$ relative over a whole run
(Tests layer).

A port of the write-back confirms the three consequences with a stand-in for the solve: the dry, momentum and
energy rows are bitwise unchanged (`[C1]`); $\rho$ is unchanged to $1.4\times10^{-16}$ relative when the solve keeps
$\sum_n y_n$ and moves by $\rho$ times its change otherwise (`[C2]`); and a cell the solve leaves alone gets $\rho_n$
back as $(\rho_n/\rho)\,\rho$, to $2.1\times10^{-16}$ relative but not always bitwise (`[C3]`).[^sat-c] The solve's own
algebra is checked by `saturation_check.py` of @sec-ch02.

[^sat-c]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch10/satadj_check.py`, output `satadj_check.out`, lines `[C1]`–`[C3]`; a numpy
    port of step (6) of `MeshBlockImpl::advance_local` at the pin, with a stand-in for kintera's solve, double
    precision.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch10-satadj-timeline places the adjustment in the step. Every stage ends its RK average with a whole-column
call of the conserved limiter, `apply_conserved_limiter_`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}). On the last stage, and only if the thermo has
reactions, the limiter runs once more and the adjustment follows
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}), so kintera never sees a negative species
density. The solve is restricted to interior cells through the `exterior(false)` part of the block
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}), and the physical ghosts are refilled from the
adjusted interior by `apply_boundaries`, after the gravity-work fixer
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}). The order of that fill relative to the exchange
and the corner refresh is @sec-ch11-timing. Every quantity here is a cell average; the adjustment is pointwise in
each cell, with no stencil.

The call passes `warm_start = true`: kintera reuses the active set of its last call when the shape and the device
match, and starts cold otherwise, `reuse`
([`kintera thermo_y.cpp:293-310`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L293-L310)).
A cell the solve could not adjust is marked by a negative diagnostic and counted; on CPU kintera also warns at once,
on CUDA the count stays on the device until snapy reads it after the step (@sec-ch10-redo).

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch10-satadj-timeline
#| fig-cap: "Where the saturation adjustment sits in one RK step. Each box is one step of the stage update, read top to bottom; the last three boxes run on the last stage only, and the final box is the driver's call after the step. Green outlines mark operations, black arrows the order."
#| fig-alt: "Six boxes in a column: stage-0 save and counter drain; per-stage limiter; last-stage limiter; UV adjustment of interior cells; boundary fill; check_redo after the step."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch10.fig_satadj_timeline import make_fig
make_fig()
```

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| step (6) gate and call | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}} | `pthermo` | reactions |
| per-stage limiter | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}} | `apply_conserved_limiter_` | `limiter` |
| boundary fill after it | {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}} | `apply_boundaries` | |
| equilibrium solve | [`kintera thermo_y.cpp:275-383`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L275-L383) | `ThermoYImpl::forward` | `uv-solver` |
| warm-start reuse | [`kintera thermo_y.cpp:293-310`](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/c55b13b2204997d2d09e04498558ab9495d8ee77/src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp#L293-L310) | `reuse` | |

: Code map of the saturation adjustment in the step. {#tbl-ch10-satadj-code}

1. The gate: last stage and a non-empty reaction list, `reactions`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).
2. The whole-column limiter, which removes negative species first, `apply_conserved_limiter_`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).
3. The state of @eq-ch10-satadj-state, `yfrac` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).
4. The module found by name, so that every equation of state with a ThermoY is served, `pthermo`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).
5. The interior-only call with the warm start ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).
6. The write-back of the species rows ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).
7. The boundary fill, `apply_boundaries` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).

The step has no setup check of its own and prints no warning; kintera's CPU warning on a failed cell is the only
message a user sees, and the redo log line of @sec-ch10-redo names the cause.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_wall_saturation.release` | energy and water over a run | $10^{-12}$ rel. | test threshold |
| `test_balance_column.release` | moist column stays at rest | $10^{-10}$ | dry case's bound |
| `test_vic_moist_device_python` | CPU equals CUDA, one step | $10^{-9}$ | the test's bound |
| `test_check_redo_saturation_python` | a failed cell redoes the step | logical | failure protocol |
| this chapter's check, `satadj_check.py` | `[C1]`-`[C3]` the write-back changes only the species rows | round-off | |

: Tests of the saturation adjustment in the step. Assertions are read from the test sources at the pin; none was
run for this draft. {#tbl-ch10-satadj-tests}

`test_wall_saturation` runs a 64 m column next to a lower and an upper wall, once condensing and once evaporating,
and asserts relative drifts of total energy and total water below $10^{-12}$ and an actual phase change
({{< code tests/test_wall_saturation.cpp WallSaturation.phase_change_preserves_energy_and_water >}}). The moist
`test_balance_column` case holds a subsaturated column, so it shows the adjustment leaves a balanced state at rest,
with the condensate row exactly zero and the vapour within $10^{-12}$, `f_balanced`
({{< code tests/test_balance_column.cpp BalanceColumn.a_moist_column_with_one_condensable_comes_out_at_rest >}}).
`test_vic_moist_device_python` compares CPU and CUDA for one moist step against the bound `DEVICE_TOL` $=10^{-9}$
({{< code tests/test_vic_moist_device.py DEVICE_TOL >}}); the gap its source comment records has no sha, deck or run
and is not quoted as evidence here. Coverage: the wall test is registered on CPU and, in CUDA builds, on CUDA; the
device test exists only in CUDA builds; no test runs the adjustment on more than one rank. Measured numbers at the
pin are **missing evidence** until a pinned build runs these entries (@sec-ch15-ch10-tests).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Only interior cells are adjusted; ghosts are copies, so a scheme that reads ghost species before the next boundary
fill sees unadjusted values. A failed cell is left unadjusted for the rest of the step and costs a redo.
:::

- The warm start is discarded whenever kintera is called with another shape or device in between, for example by
  a diagnostic call from Python; correctness is unaffected, the cost is not measured.
- Water is conserved to the phase solve's tolerance, not to round-off; the solve's tolerances are those of
  @sec-ch02-saturation.
- The switch coverage matrix (@sec-ch12-matrix) has no row for moist runs; the combinations with `SNAP_WB_REF4` and
  `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` are covered only by the moist `test_balance_column` arms
  (`test_balance_column_wb_ref4.release`, `test_balance_column_x1_centroid.release`).
